column1: DataSheet – MoSPI Reports on MPLADS
The Member of Parliament Local Area Development Scheme (MPLADS) was launched in
the year 1993 with the primary purpose of providing financial support to undertake public
works in Member of Parliament (MP) Constituencies under the corpus fund created by the
Central Government. Under this Scheme, each MP can recommend public works in their
respective district(s) of their Constituency or other districts. These proposals, if accepted,
are undertaken by respective authorities.

column1: MPLADS scheme and administration process in brief:
The main objective of the Scheme is to enable MPs, both Rajya Sabha and Lok Sabha
Members, with financial support to propose for public works developmental in nature, with
emphasis on the creation of durable community assets based on the locally felt needs of the
people.

column2: The procedure for proposing the public works by the MPS and executing the work

column1: by the authorities is detailed in the MPLADS Guidelines published by the MoSPI. The
guidelines prescribe 3-tier administrative system to implement the Scheme with MoSPI as
the Central Nodal Monitoring Authority and respective State and District Authorities as the
Implementing Authorities. In a nutshell, the procedure involves the proposal of particular
works to be done in the district(s) of the constituency from which a MP is elected or in
other districts to the District Authority. The said authority then verifies and either approves
or rejects the proposal of work. If the work is accepted, its execution is undertaken by the
district authorities. For more information on the Scheme and procedure involved, please
refer to the guidelines.
